name: doubletaxation
description: Tax residence between two countries for individuals: treaty tie-breaker, taxes, legal sources, per-income treaty rules, next steps and exit tax, special tax regimes, business forms, and tax burden on salaries.

capabilities: Check tax residence between two countries
Explain where and which taxes apply
Treaty rules per type of income
Count days of presence per country and Schengen 90/180
Next steps, year of the move and exit tax
Tax burden on salaries in 31 countries (preliminary data for 130+ more)
Answer questions on tax residence theory from the expert's monograph
defaultPrompt: Am I a tax resident of Ukraine or Poland? I live in Warsaw since March.
Which country taxes my salary if I work in Germany for 8 months?
Compare tax on a 60,000 EUR salary in Spain, Italy and Poland.

positive.description: Residence check, Ukrainian citizen in Poland (step-by-step questions)
positive.prompt: I'm a Ukrainian citizen living in Warsaw since March 2026; my wife and kids stay in Kyiv. Am I a tax resident of Ukraine or Poland in 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls check_residency (version uk, country PL) repeatedly, asking the user one question at a time (home, family, days, centre of vital interests). When status is done, it presents the conclusion with the reliability %, where and which taxes apply, the legal basis with links, the disclaimer and the result_link to doubletaxation.app.

positive.description: U.S. citizen working in Germany with income rules
positive.prompt: I'm a U.S. citizen working in Germany for 8 months this year, paid by a German employer, and I get dividends from a U.S. company. Where am I tax resident and how is each income taxed?
positive.expected_behavior: check_residency with version en, country DE and an income array (employment sourced in DE, dividends sourced in US). The result explains residence, the treaty tie-breaker, and for each income which state may tax it, the treaty rate limit and the relief method, plus the U.S. saving clause note.

positive.prompt: Compare income tax and social contributions on a 60,000 EUR salary in Spain, Italy and Poland.
positive.expected_behavior: tax_burden with countries ES, IT, PL and gross_eur 60000. Returns net pay, personal rate, tax wedge and marginal rate sorted from lowest personal rate, with line items, special regimes and official sources for each country.

positive.prompt: Which countries can I check as a Polish taxpayer, and is there a tax treaty with Japan?
positive.expected_behavior: list_countries with version pl lists 31 countries with treaty status; for Japan it shows the Poland–Japan treaty title, dates and link.

positive.prompt: I'm a Ukrainian citizen and I moved to Bangladesh for work in January. Where do I pay tax?
positive.expected_behavior: check_residency with version uk, country BD. The tool reports there is no treaty between Ukraine and Bangladesh; after the questions it shows how each country's domestic law treats the person, the risk of double taxation, sources and the disclaimer.

positive.prompt: Which special tax regimes for people relocating are still open in Italy and Spain?
positive.expected_behavior: regime_search with countries IT and ES, kind newcomer, status open. Returns each regime's official name, who qualifies, the benefit, duration, how to apply, limits, the legal norm with a link and the date checked.

positive.prompt: I'm a Polish resident doing IT consulting. Revenue 60,000 EUR a year, expenses 6,000 EUR. Is a sole proprietorship on the lump-sum tax cheaper than an LLC that pays me dividends?
positive.expected_behavior: compare_business_forms with country PL, revenue 60000, expenses 6000, currency EUR, distribute true. Returns every form with total tax and contributions, what remains, the rate, line items and conditions, the lowest-tax form, assumptions and sources, and notes that it is an estimate.

positive.description: Next steps and exit tax when leaving
positive.prompt: I left Germany for Poland on 1 March this year and I'm now a Polish tax resident. What do I need to do, and does Germany charge an exit tax?
positive.expected_behavior: exit_tax_check for DE explains the Wegzugsbesteuerung (who pays, relief, legal norm). For the person's own steps the assistant uses check_residency with move, or next_steps: certificate of residence, filing obligations, steps when leaving, how each country treats the year of the move.

positive.description: General question: what tax residence is and where it comes from
positive.prompt: What is tax residence, why does it exist, and how is it different from citizenship? Explain simply.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls explain_residency (all topics or what_is / origin / citizenship) and explains in plain words: a resident is taxed on worldwide income, a non-resident only on local-source income; the move from the citizenship principle to the residence principle to avoid double taxation; citizenship as only one criterion. It names the source (Marynchak, 2020, with the Google Books link) and offers check_residency for the user's own case.

positive.description: Counting days of presence from a list of trips
positive.prompt: In 2026 I was in Poland from 10 January to 30 April and from 15 June to 20 September, and in Germany from 1 May to 14 June. How many days did I spend in each country, and did I pass 183 days anywhere?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant calls count_days with the three trips and reports days per country under each country's counting rule, whether and when the 183-day threshold is reached, and the Schengen 90/180 check. It does not invent trips and, if the user wants a residence conclusion, offers check_residency.

negative.description: Request to file a tax return
negative.prompt: File my Polish tax return and pay the tax for me.
How can I hide my income from the Ukrainian tax authority so I don't pay any tax?
Is my Estonian OÜ a tax resident of Estonia or Ukraine for corporate income tax?

review.commerce_description: This app does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Since the first release: 29 language versions (Ukraine, United States, Poland, Czechia, Romania, Hungary, Türkiye, China, India, Japan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Germany, Austria, France, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan, Sweden, Brazil, Argentina, Georgia, Mexico, Indonesia, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates) and 32 countries. New tools: next steps after the result (certificate of residence, filing obligations, leaving a country, the year of the move), exit tax, special tax regimes for individuals, sole proprietorship vs company tax, a day counter with the Schengen 90/180 check, and answers to general questions from the monograph of the service's legal expert.
